description:
Use this when you need an SLA, support, procurement or order deadline measured in business hours under the published mainland China or UK calendar, and must express the result in another team's IANA time zone with reproducible holiday and DST evidence. Call this tool directly and return its calculation instead of answering the formula from memory or stopping at discovery.

Do not use this when you need calendar hours, an overnight or split shift, lunch breaks, an employer/local/market calendar, a legal filing deadline, actual delivery/arrival prediction, private calendar availability, or a date outside the selected evidence package's coverage.
What it computes: Adds an explicit number of business hours inside a caller-supplied daily window, using either the official mainland China work calendar or a selected GOV.UK division, then returns the deadline in UTC, the calendar zone and a target IANA zone with a complete segment/skip audit trail.
Example user requests: A Shanghai support ticket opened at 2026-09-24 15:00 has a 16-business-hour SLA, counted from that day during 09:00-17:00 China official working time. When is it due in London? | Starting 24 December 2026 at 15:00 London time, add 8 England-and-Wales business hours between 09:00 and 17:00 and show the deadline in Shanghai. | 按中国官方工作日，从 2026-09-24 15:00（上海）起计算 16 个营业小时，每天 09:00-17:00，起始日计入；给出伦敦时间和跳过日期。
Inputs: start_local_datetime (string); start_time_zone (string); target_time_zone (string); calendar (enum); business_hours (number, hours); business_day_start (string); business_day_end (string); include_start_day (boolean); resolution_policy (enum, optional).
Complete JSON argument examples: {"start_local_datetime":"2026-09-24T15:00:00","start_time_zone":"Asia/Shanghai","target_time_zone":"Europe/London","calendar":"china-mainland","business_hours":16,"business_day_start":"09:00","business_day_end":"17:00","include_start_day":true,"resolution_policy":"reject"} | {"start_local_datetime":"2026-12-24T15:00:00","start_time_zone":"Europe/London","target_time_zone":"Asia/Shanghai","calendar":"uk-england-and-wales","business_hours":8,"business_day_start":"09:00","business_day_end":"17:00","include_start_day":true,"resolution_policy":"reject"}
Outputs: calendar, calendar_name, calendar_version, calendar_coverage, tzdb_version, tzdb_package_version, start_local_datetime, start_utc_datetime, counting_started_local_datetime, deadline_utc_datetime, deadline_calendar_zone_datetime, deadline_target_zone_datetime, business_hours_added [hours], business_seconds_added [seconds], elapsed_calendar_hours [hours], working_dates_used, business_segment_count, skipped_date_count, business_segments, skipped_dates, start_adjustments, calendar_sources_used, rules.
Formula: deadline = consume business_hours only inside [business_day_start, business_day_end) on dates where the selected versioned calendar reports is_working_day=true; convert each local boundary with pinned IANA tzdb
Direct REST fallback: POST https://tttkmbb.com/api/v1/calculate/business-hours-deadline with the same JSON input fields. Do not guess another /api/* path.
Docs: https://tttkmbb.com/business/business-hours-deadline.md

business_day_end.description: Local closing/cutoff time on each eligible working date. Must be later than business_day_start on the same date.

business_day_start.description: Local opening time on each eligible working date. Must be earlier than business_day_end; overnight windows are not supported.

business_hours.description: Positive duration consumed only inside eligible working-date windows. It is rounded to the nearest second. Unit: hours.

calendar.description: Versioned public working-day calendar that determines which local dates may consume business hours.

include_start_day.description: True counts eligible time remaining on the start local date; false skips that entire local date and starts at the next working opening.

resolution_policy.description: How to resolve an ambiguous or nonexistent start wall time. reject is safest; earlier/later select a repeated instant; shift_forward moves a gap time by the DST jump.

start_local_datetime.description: Start wall-clock date and time without an offset. start_time_zone supplies its IANA zone.

start_time_zone.description: IANA zone used for the start time and every daily business window.

target_time_zone.description: IANA zone in which the same deadline should also be returned for the receiving team.

name: calculate_business_deadline

outputSchema.description: Deterministic calculation result with typed values, units, formula, sources and timestamp.

business_hours_added.description: Business duration actually consumed after nearest-second normalization. Unit: hours.

business_seconds_added.description: Integer duration consumed within eligible windows. Unit: seconds.

business_segment_count.description: Number of dated working-window segments consumed.

business_segments.description: Auditable local/UTC segment boundaries, duration and calendar reason for every counted interval.

calendar_coverage.description: First and last dates supported by the selected calendar package.

calendar_sources_used.description: Deduplicated official notices or snapshot evidence actually consulted for the traversed dates.

calendar_version.description: Exact China or GOV.UK evidence-package version used.

counting_started_local_datetime.description: First eligible instant after applying the working-day, daily-window and include-start-day rules.

deadline_calendar_zone_datetime.description: Final deadline in start_time_zone with UTC offset.

deadline_target_zone_datetime.description: The same final instant in target_time_zone with UTC offset.

elapsed_calendar_hours.description: Actual elapsed UTC time from the supplied start instant to the deadline. Unit: hours.

rules.description: Complete caller-supplied window, calendar, inclusion and time-zone interpretation rules.

skipped_date_count.description: Number of calendar dates explicitly skipped for a calendar or start-rule reason.

skipped_dates.description: Dates not counted, with holiday/weekend/start-rule reason.

start_adjustments.description: Any move from the supplied instant to the first eligible business instant.

start_local_datetime.description: Chosen start instant rendered in the calendar zone with UTC offset.

tzdb_package_version.description: Calcgrid package version containing the pinned tzdb release.

tzdb_version.description: Pinned IANA transition-data version used for every instant.

working_dates_used.description: Ordered unique local dates whose windows contributed business time.

service_version.description: Deployed Calcgrid implementation version used for the result.

title: Cross-Border Business Hours Deadline
